logic.note: The camera answers Espressif's esp32-camera driver in Jumper's simulation build: esp_camera_init finds it when camera_config_t names the GPIOs its pins are wired to (any mismatch is reported pin by pin, like a failed probe on the board), and every esp_camera_fb_get gets a frame Jumper renders (a test scene, an image, the webcam) at the frame size and pixel format the sketch set (JPEG, RGB565, grayscale, YUV422, RGB888), with the sensor_t settings applied (mirror, flip, brightness, contrast, saturation, special effects, colour bars). The pixel bus, XCLK, PCLK / VSYNC / HREF edges and the SCCB registers are not simulated: QEMU does not model the ESP32's camera interface, so the driver's API is wrapped instead.

timing.note: A capture takes about one sensor frame period on the virtual clock (60 fps up to CIF, 30 up to SVGA, 15 above at a 24 MHz XCLK, scaled with XCLK); init about 300 ms. Real frame rates also depend on JPEG size, PSRAM speed and Wi-Fi load: measure on the board.

analog.note: No image noise, exposure, white balance or lens effects: frames are clean renders of the source.

power.note: Draws a fixed 40 mA from 3V3 while powered (datasheet active figure); standby (PWDN) and the higher current at UXGA are not modelled. Over 3.6 V on 3V3 is an error (5 V damages it).

emulates: Detection by esp_camera_init on the GPIOs it is wired to (pins checked one by one)
Frames at every esp32-camera frame size up to UXGA, in JPEG / RGB565 / grayscale / YUV422 / RGB888
sensor_t settings (frame size, format, quality, mirror, flip, brightness, contrast, saturation, special effect, colour bars)
doesNotEmulate: The DVP pixel bus, XCLK, PCLK / VSYNC / HREF timing and DMA
SCCB register reads and writes (set_reg changes nothing)
Exposure, white balance, noise, blur and lens distortion
testOnRealDevice: Picture quality and exposure in your light
Wire length: the pixel bus runs at 10 to 20 MHz, keep it short (under about 10 cm) or frames tear
Frame rate with your frame size, JPEG quality and Wi-Fi
That the pins you chose are free (not flash / PSRAM / strapping pins)
